name: Western Big Game Seasonal Habitat and Migration Corridors Fund
summary: Grants for restoring elk, mule deer and pronghorn seasonal habitat, stopover areas and migration corridors in western states, such as fence modification and sagebrush restoration. A separate option is open only to states and Tribes.

geography.label: Focal areas in 11 western states (18 states for Option B)

amount.note: Option A: most competitive grants are at least this much, with no maximum request

status.quote: Full Proposal Due Date April 21, 2026, 11:59 PM ET

deadline.quote: Full Proposal Due Date April 21, 2026, 11:59 PM ET

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, U.S. Federal government agencies, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal Governments and organizations, and educational institutions.

geography.quote: Only projects proposed in focal areas identified by states under SO 3362 in 11 western states (depicted in green) and Native Nations within Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming will be eligible.

access.quote: is soliciting proposals for projects that improve the quality of ungulate seasonal habitat, stopover areas, and migration corridors

amount.quote: The most competitive grants will be at least $100,000 and there is no maximum request amount.

co_finance_required.quote: A minimum 1:1 non-federal match is required as in-kind or cash contributions.
